categories.playbook: Maven Central refuses plain http since 2020-01-15. Change every http:// repository/pluginRepository URL for Central (repo.maven.apache.org, repo1.maven.org, central.maven.org) to https://repo.maven.apache.org/maven2 in the POMs (and parent POMs in the reactor). If the http URL comes from an old Maven's built-in super POM (Maven < 3.2.3) or a settings.xml, add an https <repository>/<pluginRepository> with id 'central' to the root POM, which overrides the built-in one.

patterns: Remote host closed connection during handshake
categories.playbook: The JVM running Maven cannot negotiate TLS with the repository (JDK 7 defaults to TLSv1; Central requires TLSv1.2). Run Maven on a newer JDK (compile level is set by maven.compiler.source/target, not by the JDK running Maven), or pass -Dhttps.protocols=TLSv1.2 (persist it in .mvn/jvm.config or MAVEN_OPTS). If artifacts are already in ~/.m2, try offline mode (-o).

patterns: has not been downloaded from it before
categories.playbook: Offline mode (-o, or <offline>true</offline> in settings.xml) and the artifact is not in ~/.m2. Drop -o if the network works; otherwise the build must use an artifact/version that is already cached: list ~/.m2/repository/<group path>/<artifact>/ and align the POM version to one that exists.

patterns: Plugin .* or one of its dependencies could not be resolved
Failed to read artifact descriptor for .*plugin
categories.playbook: A plugin (or its version) cannot be resolved. Pin an explicit, published plugin version in <pluginManagement> of the root POM (missing versions make Maven pick one from metadata). Check the coordinates (groupId defaults to org.apache.maven.plugins only for maven-*-plugin), the pluginRepositories URL (https), and whether the version exists in ~/.m2 when offline. 'No plugin found for prefix' means the plugin is not declared or its groupId is not searchable; invoke as groupId:artifactId:version:goal or declare it.

patterns: was cached in the local repository, resolution will not be reattempted
categories.playbook: A dependency, parent POM, or BOM cannot be resolved. Find the exact coordinates in the error. Causes, in order: (1) a version that does not exist or an external -SNAPSHOT/range/LATEST that no longer resolves -> pin a published version; (2) a sibling reactor module not built yet -> build from the root with -am or install it first (reactor order); (3) repository URL http or dead -> https / correct repo; (4) 'cached in the local repository, resolution will not be reattempted' -> rerun with -U or delete that artifact's folder in ~/.m2; (5) parent POM relativePath wrong. Duplicate classes from two artifacts (NoSuchMethodError, LinkageError at test time) mean a missing exclusion. Use mvn dependency:tree -Dverbose -Dincludes=<groupId> to see who pulls it in; exclude a broken transitive with <exclusions> (comment why) or force a version in <dependencyManagement>.

The POM model itself is invalid. Fix the reported line: missing dependency version (add it, or add a dependencyManagement/BOM entry), duplicate declarations (remove one; banDuplicatePomDependencyVersions), a <module> that points at a missing directory, an undefined ${property}, or XML syntax. Check the effective POM with mvn help:effective-pom once it parses.

patterns: The projects in the reactor contain a cyclic reference
Could not find the selected project in the reactor
categories.playbook: Reactor problem: a dependency cycle between modules (break it by moving shared code into a common module) or a -pl/-rf selector that names no module (use :artifactId or the module path). Module order follows dependencies, not the <modules> list order.

patterns: Detected Maven Version: .* is not in the allowed range
categories.playbook: The installed Maven is outside the range a plugin or the enforcer requires. Use the Maven wrapper if present (./mvnw), or pick plugin versions compatible with the installed Maven (mvn -v); widening an enforcer requireMavenVersion range is a last resort and must be justified.

patterns: has been compiled by a more recent version
Source option .* is no longer supported
Target option .* is no longer supported
Detected JDK Version: .* is not in the allowed range
categories.playbook: The JDK running Maven does not match the project's language level or a dependency's bytecode. Read maven.compiler.source/target/release and the original CI's jdk. Switch the JDK (in this container: source /opt/jdk_switcher/jdk_switcher.sh && jdk_switcher use openjdk8 | openjdk7 | oraclejdk8, or export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/<dir> and PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH). 'compiled by a more recent version'/'Unsupported major.minor' means a dependency or plugin needs a newer JDK than the one running: either run on a newer JDK or pin the older dependency/plugin version that matches. JDK 9+ removed javax.xml.bind/javax.annotation from the default classpath; JDK 12+ dropped source/target 6, JDK 9+ needs release instead of bootclasspath tricks.

An annotation processor failed or could not load. If the project itself provides processors (e.g. google/auto value/factory/service), a processor error during the module's own compile usually means the processor code or its META-INF/services/javax.annotation.processing.Processor registration is wrong, or the processor jar is on its own compile path (-proc:none is set for processor modules in some builds). If the project consumes processors, check annotationProcessorPaths in maven-compiler-plugin and the processor's version vs the JDK. Error text with a file:line points at the generated or annotated source; read the processor message literally.

patterns: is not abstract and does not override
class .* is public, should be declared in a file named
categories.playbook: javac errors. Read the first [ERROR] /path/File.java:[line,col] message, not the cascade. cannot find symbol/package does not exist -> a missing import, a renamed API in a dependency version, a missing dependency or wrong <scope> (test-scope dep used from main code; provided not on test path), or a sibling module not rebuilt (build from root with -am). Signature mismatches after a dependency upgrade -> adapt the code to the dependency version actually resolved (mvn dependency:tree), or pin the version the code was written for. A dependency marked <optional>true</optional> (or provided/test scope) in another module is not transitive: declare it where it is used. Errors naming classes that no longer exist in source point at stale target/ output: make sure the command includes clean. testCompile failures are in src/test; compile failures in src/main. Fix the code; do not exclude the file from compilation.

patterns: The forked VM terminated without properly saying goodbye
There was an error in the forked process
categories.playbook: The surefire fork JVM crashed or exited. Look at the dump files (target/surefire-reports/*.dump*). Causes: OOM in the fork (raise -Xmx in surefire <argLine>), System.exit in a test, an argLine flag the running JDK rejects (e.g. -XX:MaxPermSize removed on JDK 8+ is only a warning, but --add-opens fails on JDK 8), or an old surefire (<2.22) on a newer JDK. Pin a surefire version that supports the JDK.

Tests ran and failed. Open target/surefire-reports/<TestClass>.txt for each failing test and read the assertion message and stack. Decide whether the production code or the test is wrong given the commit's intent (git log -1, git show). Re-run one test fast: mvn -B test -pl :<module> -am -Dtest=<Class>#<method> -DfailIfNoTests=false (surefire 2.x) / -Dsurefire.failIfNoSpecifiedTests=false (3.x). Watch for environment-sensitive tests (locale, timezone, file ordering, JDK-specific toString/hash ordering, compiler message text that differs across JDKs). Never pass -DskipTests or -Dmaven.test.skip=true, add @Ignore, or delete a test to get green.

An enforcer rule failed. dependencyConvergence/requireUpperBoundDeps: run mvn dependency:tree -Dverbose -Dincludes=<groupId>:<artifactId>, then force one version in <dependencyManagement> (nearest definition wins otherwise) or add an <exclusion>. bannedDependencies: exclude the banned artifact where it enters. requireJavaVersion/requireMavenVersion: change the JDK/Maven, not the rule.

Javadoc generation failed (JDK 8+ doclint is strict). Fix the reported javadoc errors in source, or configure the javadoc plugin with <doclint>none</doclint> (JDK 8+) / <additionalparam>-Xdoclint:none</additionalparam> (old plugin versions); a pinned plugin version that matches the JDK matters. -Dmaven.javadoc.skip=true is acceptable only if the original CI command used it.

patterns: Coverage checks have not been met
Some files do not have the expected license header
categories.playbook: A quality gate (checkstyle, PMD, SpotBugs, JaCoCo coverage, animal-sniffer API signature, license header, formatter) failed. Fix the reported violations in the code (animal-sniffer 'Undefined reference' means code uses an API newer than the target JDK signature: use an older API). Do not lower thresholds or disable the plugin unless the failure is environmental.

Resource filtering or encoding failure. Binary files are being filtered (split resources: filtering=true only for *.properties/*.xml, or list nonFilteredFileExtensions), or the source/resource encoding is unset (set project.build.sourceEncoding=UTF-8; LANG=C in the container makes the platform default ASCII).

Out of memory. Raise heap for Maven (MAVEN_OPTS=-Xmx2g, persist in .mvn/jvm.config), for forked compilers (maven-compiler-plugin <fork>true</fork> with <compilerArgs><arg>-J-Xmx512m</arg></compilerArgs> / <maxmem>), or for test forks (surefire <argLine>-Xmx1024m</argLine>). Reduce parallelism (-T, surefire forkCount/parallel). PermGen on JDK 7: -XX:MaxPermSize=256m.

A packaging/installation plugin failed. war without web.xml -> <failOnMissingWebXml>false</failOnMissingWebXml>; shade -> filters for META-INF/*.SF|*.DSA|*.RSA and ServicesResourceTransformer; gpg signing should live in a release profile, not the default build; deploy needs distributionManagement + credentials and normally is not part of a CI verification build.
